_doc: Asia at the resolution the continent deserves — the imperial capitals and mountain country the first pass skipped, the volcano and cave landscapes, and the second cities of Japan, Korea and India.

destinations.name: Xi'an & the Terracotta Army
destinations.blurb: Eight thousand clay soldiers still standing in their pits outside a city that was the eastern end of the Silk Road — plus intact Ming walls you can cycle right around and a Muslim Quarter that cooks until late.

destinations.name: Zhangjiajie & Fenghuang
destinations.blurb: Sandstone pillars standing out of the mist — the landscape that Avatar borrowed — with glass walkways bolted to the cliffs, and downriver the stilt-house town of Fenghuang lit up on the water at night.

destinations.name: Takayama & the Japan Alps
destinations.blurb: Edo-era merchant streets preserved in dark timber, morning markets on the river, and an hour away the thatched farmhouses of Shirakawa-go under deep snow — with the Alps and their onsen towns all around.

destinations.name: Naoshima & the Seto Inland Sea
destinations.blurb: Fishing islands turned over to contemporary art — Tadao Ando's concrete museums half-buried in hillsides, a Monet room lit only by daylight, and Kusama's yellow pumpkin on the jetty.

destinations.name: Nara & Koyasan
destinations.blurb: Japan's first capital, where deer bow for biscuits under the largest bronze Buddha in the world — and south of it Koyasan, a mountaintop of 117 temples where you sleep in one and walk a lantern-lit necropolis at night.

destinations.name: Mumbai
destinations.blurb: India at full volume — Victorian Gothic and Art Deco along the same seafront, the dabbawalas' lunch relay, Elephanta's rock-cut caves across the harbour, and Bollywood underwriting the whole performance.

destinations.name: Amritsar & Punjab
destinations.blurb: The Golden Temple floating on its tank, gold leaf doubled in the water, with a kitchen beside it that feeds a hundred thousand people a day for nothing — and at the border, the theatrical evening ceremony at Wagah.

destinations.name: Darjeeling & Sikkim
destinations.blurb: Tea gardens falling away below a ridge, a toy train still running on two-foot gauge, and on a clear morning Kangchenjunga — third highest on earth — filling the whole northern sky from Tiger Hill.

destinations.name: Phong Nha & the Caves
destinations.blurb: The largest cave passage on earth is here — Son Doong, with its own jungle and clouds inside — and around it a karst national park of river caves, ziplines and a valley of near-empty homestays.

destinations.name: The Mekong Delta
destinations.blurb: Nine river mouths and a landscape that is more water than land — the floating market at Cái Răng trading from boat to boat before dawn, coconut-candy workshops on the creeks, and homestays down channels too narrow for cars.

destinations.name: Khao Sok
destinations.blurb: Rainforest older than the Amazon, and at its heart Cheow Lan lake — limestone towers rising straight out of jade water, with floating raft houses tied beneath them and gibbons calling at first light.

destinations.name: Sukhothai & Ayutthaya
destinations.blurb: Two former capitals left as ruin parks — Sukhothai's serene walking Buddhas among lotus ponds, best seen by bicycle at dawn, and Ayutthaya's brick prangs with a Buddha head grown into a fig tree's roots.

destinations.name: Bromo & Ijen
destinations.blurb: East Java's two great volcanoes — Bromo smoking inside a sea of ash you cross at 4am for the sunrise, and Ijen, where sulphur miners climb out with baskets and the crater burns with blue flame before dawn.

destinations.name: Lake Toba & Sumatra
destinations.blurb: The largest volcanic lake on earth, filling a caldera left by an eruption that nearly finished us off — with Samosir island in the middle, Batak villages and boat-prowed roofs, and orangutans in the jungle at Bukit Lawang.

destinations.name: Banaue & the Cordilleras
destinations.blurb: Two thousand years of rice terraces cut into the Cordillera by hand and still farmed — Batad's amphitheatre is the one to walk into — plus Sagada's hanging coffins on the limestone cliffs beyond.

destinations.name: Coron & Busuanga
destinations.blurb: A Japanese wartime fleet sunk in shallow water and now grown over with coral — the best wreck diving in Southeast Asia — plus Kayangan Lake between limestone walls, rated the cleanest lake in the country.

destinations.name: Melaka
destinations.blurb: Portuguese, Dutch and British in turn, layered over a Malay port and a Peranakan merchant class — red Dutch Square, shophouses on Jonker Street, and a Nyonya kitchen you will not find done better anywhere.

destinations.name: Busan
destinations.blurb: Korea's port city, built up the sides of hills — the Gamcheon culture village painted in blocks of colour, Jagalchi fish market where you pick it live, and city beaches that fill shoulder to shoulder in August.

destinations.name: Gyeongju
destinations.blurb: A thousand years of Silla capital left as grass-covered royal tombs sitting between the streets — plus Bulguksa temple and the Seokguram grotto Buddha watching the sunrise over the East Sea from his hillside.

destinations.name: Khiva
destinations.blurb: A walled desert city you can walk around the top of — the Itchan Kala is small enough to cross in twenty minutes and dense enough to hold fifty monuments, including a fat turquoise minaret that was never finished.
